title: Anthropic创纪录IPO募资1048亿美元，七位联合创始人套现近20亿美元
content:
On November 19, the AI lab Anthropic officially went public, raising a total of $104.8 billion (or up to $117 billion if underwriters fully exercise their over-allotment option), significantly breaking the $16 billion tech IPO record set by Facebook in 2012.
The offering was priced at $83 per share, above the $74 midpoint of its initial price range. In addition to Class A common stock, the company sold $26 billion of non-voting Class N shares to tech giants, with Nvidia and Google each subscribing to $10 billion, and the remainder taken by AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC.
With the listing, Anthropic's seven co-founders cashed out a combined $1.95 billion. At $83 per share, the roughly 3.4 million shares each subscribed to were worth about $280 million before taxes, about $30 million more than expected based on the $74 price.
In addition, the IPO filing shows that each founder voluntarily expressed an intention to donate 80% of their personal equity to charity, but the commitment is not legally binding and can be revoked at any time. Regarding ownership structure, Google and Amazon together hold 28% of Anthropic, with stakes of 13.4% and 14.6% respectively; if Amazon fully converts the promissory notes obtained from its earlier investment, its stake will approach 24%.
Although the listing expanded Anthropic's available working capital to nearly $230 billion, the high underlying computing costs still create enormous financial pressure.
As of September 30, 2026, the company's compute and infrastructure spending commitments for the next 12 months had reached $70.7 billion, and it must fulfill a cumulative $451.6 billion by the end of 2030; adding other conditional or not-yet-priced long-term agreements, its total foreseeable infrastructure investment is as high as $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion. This enormous funding demand shows that even after completing an epic fundraising, leading AI companies remain deeply tied to the capital-intensive compute arms race.

report.summary: Anthropic上市募资1048亿美元，创科技IPO新纪录
report.background: Anthropic 2021年由前OpenAI成员创立，靠Claude系列模型跻身第一梯队。大模型训练与推理的算力开销远超一级市场融资能力，OpenAI、xAI等同行也在争夺巨额资本，上市成为头部AI公司补充资金的必然选择。英伟达、谷歌、微软、台积电等既是股东又是芯片与云服务供应商，形成典型的“循环投资”结构。此次IPO打破Facebook 2012年160亿美元的纪录，标志生成式AI公司正式进入公开市场接受散户与机构定价。
key_points: 发行价83美元高于区间中值74美元，总募资1048亿美元，超额配售可达1170亿，远超Facebook 2012年160亿美元纪录。
同时向科技巨头出售260亿美元无投票权N类股：英伟达、谷歌各认购100亿，AMD、博通、美光、微软、台积电分摊其余。
七位联合创始人合计套现19.5亿美元，人均约2.8亿美元；虽表态捐出80%个人股权做慈善，但无法律约束力、可随时撤回。
股权上谷歌持13.4%、亚马逊持14.6%合计28%，若亚马逊将早期投资的可转债全部转股，持股将逼近24%。
资金到位不等于安全：未来12个月算力承诺707亿美元，2030年前累计4516亿，可预见基础设施投入高达1.05万亿至1.08万亿美元。
上市使可用营运资金增至近2300亿美元，但算力支出承诺的规模说明“募资—买卡—再募资”的循环仍难打破。
report.impact: 对AI行业：头部实验室从私募市场走向公开市场，算力竞赛被彻底金融化，供应商与股东身份重叠的“循环投资”将成为监管与投资者审视焦点。对开发者：Claude生态资金更充裕、模型迭代或加快，但上市公司需向股东交代回报，API定价与免费额度可能收紧。对普通用户：能力红利与订阅涨价并存，同时个人养老金和指数基金将被动持有AI股票，泡沫破裂风险传导到散户。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注Claude API与Claude Code、Anthropic主导的MCP（模型上下文协议）、AWS Bedrock与Google Vertex AI托管入口；同时跟踪英伟达、台积电、美光财报中的数据中心订单，以及后续S-1/10-Q披露的算力承诺数据。
